citation.title: Policy Misperceptions and Support for Gun Control Legislation

standing_assumptions: The letter prints no variance formula. These are audit reconstruction identities for accepted P054-N001, conditional on fixed binary responses, positive survey weights and the stated independent-respondent linearisation. They do not establish historical procedure, full survey-design validity or national 95% coverage. The original data weights, nine interval reconstructions and historical-procedure report are empirical/provenance inputs rather than Lean conclusions. The author reports intercept-only classical weighted least squares in R; independent identification of its historical use remains absent.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Audit reconstruction: weighted-ratio residual and linearisation identities
canonical_claim.location: Letter p.223; audit P054-N001, final Evidence formulas
canonical_claim.statement: For N≥2 observations, d_i∈{0,1}, y_i∈{0,1}, w_i>0, n=sum d_i>0, W=sum d_i w_i and pHat=sum d_i w_i y_i/W, let z_i=d_i w_i(y_i−pHat). Then sum z_i=0 and [sum z_i^2/(N(N−1))]/(W/N)^2 = [N/(N−1)] sum d_i w_i^2(y_i−pHat)^2/W^2. With equal weights, sum d_i w_i^2(y_i−pHat)^2/W^2=pHat(1−pHat)/n; hence V=N/(N−1) times V0. No general inequality V≥V0 is asserted for unequal weights.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: d: group membership/valid response; y: binary answer; w: fixed positive weight; N: full respondent count; n: group count; W: group weight; pHat: weighted ratio.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: Finite weighted binary-response algebra; denominator nonzero follows from n>0 and positive weights.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Audit reconstruction: classical intercept-only weighted least-squares variance
canonical_claim.location: Letter p.223; audit P054-N001, final Evidence classical-WLS formula
canonical_claim.statement: Under the finite binary/positive-weight setting of T1 and n≥2, the weighted squared residual sum equals W*pHat*(1−pHat). For an intercept-only weighted least-squares fit with classical variance RSS_w/((n−1)W), the variance is pHat*(1−pHat)/(n−1), equal to n/(n−1) times V0. This algebra demonstrates compatibility of the author-reported method with the matching calculation, not independently established historical use or validity of inverse-variance assumptions.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: As in T1; RSS_w=sum d_i w_i(y_i−pHat)^2; V0=pHat(1−pHat)/n.
